cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus (2 Corinthians 1:1), is writing to the church in Corinth about a return visit he planned and didn't make. He opens with a boast about how he's lived among them. His own conscience is taking the stand as his character witness.

cards.question: Paul says he's lived among the Corinthians in holiness and sincerity from God. He says he didn't run on worldly wisdom. So what did he run on?
Paul's talking about the letters he sends to Corinth. True or false: he says he writes them things beyond their ability to read and understand.

cards.text: Paul says they've understood him in part, and he hopes they'll understand him completely. Being half-understood is like getting half a cookie recipe, and friend, the half you got just says “preheat.”

cards.question: Paul looks ahead to the day of our Lord Jesus. What does he hope he and the Corinthians will do on that day?

cards.text: Confident of all that, Paul made a plan: stop in Corinth on the way to Macedonia, then swing back through Corinth on the way out. Two visits, one trip, and friend, the man had an ITINERARY.

cards.question: Paul planned to visit Corinth first so they might receive a ___ blessing.
After his second stop in Corinth, Paul wanted the church to help send him on his way. Where was he headed?

cards.text: Then Paul asks: did he make that plan carelessly, or plan by human standards, saying “Yes, yes” and also “No, no”? Baker, that's me and the snooze button: YES I'm up, NO I'm not, YES I'm up, no I'm NOT.

cards.question: Paul's asking whether his word flips back and forth. True or false: he says his message to the Corinthians is “Yes” and “No.”

cards.text: Then Paul points to the One that he and his fellow preachers Silvanus and Timothy proclaimed in Corinth: Jesus Christ, the Son of God. Jesus was never “Yes” and “No,” but in Him it has always been “Yes.”

cards.question: Paul says ___ the promises of God are “Yes” in Christ.

cards.text: So through Jesus, our “Amen” is spoken to the glory of God. And Paul says it's God who establishes both him and the Corinthians in Christ.

cards.question: Paul writes that God put something in “our hearts” as a pledge of what is to come. What is it?
Paul lists more of what God has done. True or false: Paul writes that God “anointed us” and “placed His seal on us.”

cards.text: Now Paul calls God as his witness about why he didn't come back to Corinth. When a man brings THAT witness, friend, you put the cookie down and listen.

cards.question: Why does Paul say he didn't return to Corinth?
Paul says he doesn't lord it over their faith. Instead, he and his team are fellow ___ with them for their joy.

cards.text: Paul stayed away to spare the Corinthians, and now he says he made up his mind about visiting them again. And unlike me at the topping station, once Paul's mind is made up, it STAYS made up.

cards.question: Paul decided not to make another ___ visit to the Corinthians.

cards.text: Then Paul asks a question. If he grieves the church, who's left to cheer him up?

cards.question: If Paul grieves the Corinthians, who does he say is left to cheer him?

cards.text: So instead of coming, Paul wrote them. He says he was confident in all of them, that they'd share his joy.

cards.question: True or false: Paul wrote so that when he arrived, he wouldn't be grieved by the people who ought to make him rejoice.

cards.text: And that letter wasn't easy, baker: Paul wrote it out of great distress and anguish of heart, through many tears. The only time I cry in this bakery is when I open the oven door too fast and the steam gets me, so I'm not even in the same LEAGUE.

cards.question: Paul wrote that letter through many tears. What does he say it was meant to show the Corinthians?

answers.text: How angry he was with them

cards.text: Now Paul says that if anyone has caused grief, here's how things stand. Paul never names anyone, and neither will I.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the person who caused grief has mostly grieved Paul.

cards.text: The majority of the church already punished this man, and Paul says it's sufficient for him. When the timer dings, friend, you don't argue with the timer.

cards.question: What does Paul say the church ought to do for this man now?
Paul says to forgive and comfort the man so he won't be overwhelmed by excessive ___.

cards.text: So Paul urges them to reaffirm their love for him. When that scared can opener slid into my drawer, sure it had done something wrong, it didn't need a lecture, friend; it needed somebody to say, “Let me show you around.”
Then Paul tells them why he wrote that letter: it was a test, to see if they'd do what he asked.

cards.question: Paul says his purpose in writing was to see if they'd stand the test and be ___ in everything.

cards.text: And Paul's right there with them. Whoever they forgive, he forgives too.

cards.question: Paul says that if he has forgiven anything, he forgave it for the church's sake, in the presence of someone. Who?
Paul says his forgiving is in order that someone should not outwit them. Who?
True or false: Paul says they are unaware of Satan's schemes.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 15 quotes "placed His seal on us.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card cites only 2 Corinthians 1:12, but it also tells about a return visit Paul planned and didn't make (1:15-16, 1:23). It also says Paul "opens with" the boast, but the letter opens at 1:1, and 1:12 continues from 1:3-11.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Jesus was never 'Yes' and 'No'" adds a time word. The text says He "was not 'Yes' and 'No.'"

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The joke says once Paul's mind is made up "it STAYS made up." The passage is about Paul changing his travel plans (1:15-17, 1:23), so the text shows this is wrong. It is also an exaggeration about Paul, not about Papa Dorin.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "this man" points back to card 11, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say who the man is: the one who caused grief and was punished by the majority.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "the man" doesn't say who he is: the one who caused grief and was punished.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "to see if they'd do what he asked" gives away the answer to card 16 ("obedient"). It also adds "what he asked," while 2:9 says only "obedient in everything."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
